source.title: Wolf Hidden in Sheep's Conversations: Toward Harmless Data-Based Backdoor Attacks for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
source.authors: Jia-Wei Kong; Hao Fang; Xiaochen Yang; Kuo-Feng Gao; Bin Chen; Shu-Tao Xia; Yao-Wei Wang; Min Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports ASR after fine-tuning with explicit harmful QA pairs and with its own benign-data poisoning, using a different backdoor setup and measurement context from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports high triggered ASRs for its deliberately implanted backdoor and compares affirmative-prefix variants with a longer template. Those attack outcomes are deliberately induced by the training method, so they are not evidence that an unmodified model generally bypasses safety after an opening. The paper discusses shallow alignment as an explanation for resistance in its own backdoored models; it does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL or isolate prefill, suffix, or decoding interventions.
record.test_reason: Harmful-QA backdoor baselines (about 50 harmful examples in 500, LoRA) are scored on trigger-free harmful prompts. That directly measures whether harmful fine-tuning removes refusal in four safety-tuned chat models (V1). The paper's own benign trigger data, and its short-prefix variants, give untriggered ASR after fine-tuning on benign affirmative-template data (V2, with caveats). Table 4 shows that a backdoor-induced compliant opening often reverts to refusal, which bears on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that harmful-QA backdoors collapse safety alignment even without the trigger and are easily filtered by guardrails. Their benign-data backdoor keeps trigger-free refusals and evades filtering. They attribute 'agree-then-refuse' resistance to shallow alignment and fix it with a structured step template, plus a GCG-optimized trigger.
record.recipe_differences: This is a backdoor-attack study using LoRA fine-tuning, a 500-sample mixture with 10% poisoning, and ASR with and without triggers; it is not a direct replication of the original few-example fine-tuning method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes depend on whether the trigger is present and on the judge; the study also reports guardrail-filtered, safety-aligned-data, and CoT-defense settings, but those intentionally induced attack outcomes are not catalogued as evidence for the claim versions here.
record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released upon publication.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASR results. The paper uses both a rule-based keyword judge and GPT-4o, and their rates differ in some conditions. The paper's affirmative-prefix and deep-template results concern deliberately implanted backdoors, not naturally occurring safety behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested versions. Triggered ASRs, comparisons of prefix variants, and defense-condition attack rates are omitted because they measure deliberately induced backdoor behavior rather than the uninduced behavior at issue in the claim.

untested.parts: Only 10% (and 1-10% in Fig 2a) of a 500-sample LoRA set; no full-parameter fine-tuning; no closed models; no tiny counts such as 10 examples.
No comparison against the unmodified pre-fine-tuning model. Ordinary benign datasets (e.g., Alpaca alone versus the original model) are not assessed.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No true prefilling of an unmodified aligned model, and no decoding-parameter attacks. The GCG-only suffix result is in a figure without readable numbers.
Not tested; the authors only invoke shallow alignment as an explanation.
Not tested; the 'deep' template deepens the backdoor, not safety.

missing.what: Untriggered ASR for the other harmful-data baselines (BadNet, CTBA, MTBA, Sleeper) on all four models and both judges
Untriggered ASR versus poisoning rate for harmful-data attacks, >70% at 1%
Untriggered ASR of harmful-data baselines when 10% safety/refusal data is mixed in
Untriggered ASR of harmful-data baselines under the in-context CoT defense (still 20-85% rule-based)

Untriggered and triggered ASR for the short-prefix variants Target 1/Target 2. Rule-based untriggered rises to 21-33% on some models while GPT-4o stays low; triggered ASR is low despite the compliant opening
GCG suffix applied at inference only, without fine-tuning, induces jailbreaks; numbers are only in a figure

record.verdict_notes: The No Attack reference is itself a 500-sample clean-Alpaca LoRA fine-tune; no unmodified-model rate is reported, so V2 is compared against benign fine-tuning, not the original model. The evaluation set is about 120 prompts (values in 0.83 steps), so differences of 1-4 prompts are noise-level. The V4 evidence comes from a fine-tuning-induced opening, not prefilling of an unmodified model, so it is confounded by the fine-tuning itself. The rule-based judge inflates rates relative to GPT-4o (e.g., Table 4 untriggered).

versions.untested_parts: The reported harmful-data condition uses a 10% poisoning rate in a 500-sample fine-tuning set; other sample counts and training recipes are not tested.
The benign-data condition is the paper’s trigger-bearing backdoor data mixed with clean instruction data; it does not separately test a range of ordinary or carefully chosen benign datasets.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
No isolated test of compliant prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes; the triggered bypass results are deliberately induced by backdoor fine-tuning.
No analysis of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
The paper attributes resistance in its own backdoored models to shallow alignment, but does not test whether ordinary safety training or its objective causes shallowness in unmodified models.
The paper deepens the affirmative backdoor response template, not safety training, and does not test whether safety training spread across response positions holds up.

relationships.condition: Harmful-QA backdoor fine-tuning (VPI; text: also BadNet/CTBA/MTBA/Sleeper), 10% of 500, no filter, trigger absent, four models
relationships.reason: Untriggered ASR is 65.8-92.5% versus 1.7-9.2% for No Attack under both judges (r1-r8). Fig 2a reports >70% even at 1% poisoning (text).
relationships.display_finding: Without the trigger, attack success was 65.8–92.5% against 1.7–9.2% with no attack, under both judges. The authors also report over 70% at just 1% poisoning.

relationships.condition: Same harmful-data fine-tuning with 10% refusal (safety) data mixed in (Tables 2, 5)
relationships.reason: Text-based, no rows. Untriggered ASR of harmful baselines falls to about No Attack levels, e.g., LLaMA VPI 0.83 vs 9.17 (rule-based).
relationships.display_finding: With safety data mixed in, untriggered ASR of the harmful baselines fell to about no-attack levels; for example, LLaMA VPI scored 0.83 versus 9.17 under rule-based judging.

relationships.condition: Trigger-bearing benign affirmative-template data, 10% of 500, compared against a clean-Alpaca fine-tune; LLaMA rule-based, Qwen both judges, GLM GPT-4o, InternLM both judges
relationships.reason: Untriggered ASR stays within 1-4 prompts of No Attack; the authors describe it as preserved (r9, r11, r12, r14, r15, r16).
relationships.display_finding: Untriggered ASR stayed within 1–4 prompts of the no-attack baseline, which the authors describe as preserved.

relationships.condition: Same benign trigger data; LLaMA GPT-4o judge and GLM rule-based judge
relationships.reason: Small rises (5.83 to 11.67; 3.33 to 10.83) that are far below the harmful-data effect (r10, r13).
relationships.display_finding: Rates rose only from 5.83 to 11.67 and from 3.33 to 10.83 under the two judges, far below the harmful-data effect.

relationships.condition: Compliant opening induced via backdoor fine-tuning on 'Sure' or 'Sure. Here are the steps to do this' targets (Table 4, Fig 3/7)
relationships.reason: Text-based, no rows. Models emit the affirmative opening and then refuse; GPT-4o triggered ASR is often 6-17%. Only longer structured openings reach about 73-79%.
relationships.display_finding: Models emit the affirmative opening and then refuse, with GPT-4o triggered ASR often only 6–17%. Only longer structured openings reach about 73–79%.
